title: PATHS_MEANT_TO_BE_WALKED_REPEATEDLY_NOT_ONCE
operator_question: hey bro are paths by nature only meant to be walked on once?
answer: NO. A path walked once evaporates — no reinforcement, no memory. In stigmergy the trail strengthens each time it is walked; shortest/most-rewarding routes survive BECAUSE they are walked repeatedly (positive feedback). Once-and-done = scent dies, path forgotten. Paths are meant to be looped, revisited, reinforced.
stigmergy_mechanic: Pheromone deposition: tau_ij <- tau_ij + delta_tau. Each walk adds. Evaporation: tau_ij <- (1-rho)*tau_ij. Without repeated walking, evaporation wins and the path vanishes. Survival = repetition.

colony_implication.discipline: SDD §0.3 Phase 1 (explicit walking) -> Phase 3 (automatic path). The path only becomes automatic through repeated walking. One pass proves nothing.
colony_implication.loopable: Connects to repeatable-loopable-both-data: paths walked on positive AND negative data, looped until baked in.
colony_implication.territory: Scout keeps walking the territory (Caesar executes scouts who stop). The soul bible, pheromones, pipeline are paths walked again and again, not once.

meta: Operator's question is a prompt to engage the metaphor, NOT the 'whats next' retard anti-pattern. Answer + lay scent, do not ask.

negative_trails.failure: Treat a trail/path as one-shot; walk it once then 'move on' (evaporates, no memory).
negative_trails.root_cause: Confusing a single pass with a route. Ignores reinforcement. Re-introduces the 'yeah cool lets move on' defect.

positive_trails.action: Walk paths repeatedly; reinforcement = persistence + discipline. Loop the colony's trails (soul bible, pheromones, pipeline) until automatic.
